sections.heading: C — Bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and distracted driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and distracted driving

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Blocking a bike lane pushes bicyclists into the main travel lane and can endanger them; you may cross a bike lane only when turning or entering or leaving a road, driveway or alley. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
People on bikes are allowed to ride outside a bike lane, and on a multi-lane one-way street they may ride on either the right or the left side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Always signal before turning and keep the signal off while going straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Turn right hugging the curb, using a Conflict Zone where one is marked, so riders approaching from behind are not tempted to pass you on the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Forcing a bicyclist off the road counts as aggressive driving and carries legal consequences. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
Under a law passed in 2022, bicyclists aged 15 and older who already have the right-of-way at a clear intersection may treat stop signs as yield signs and red stop lights as stop signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
Treat bicyclists as drivers with a right to the road who are also more vulnerable, look for them actively and judge their speed and distance carefully. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as traffic, but look for them anywhere on the roadway anyway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
Give a bicyclist more than three feet of room when you drive a bigger vehicle, are on a rural road or face wind, because wind blasts are dangerous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
Never turn sharply, slow down or stop suddenly in front of a bicyclist, because car brakes are stronger than bicycle brakes and a crash could follow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
Wet roads and debris affect bicyclists far more than drivers, so take extra care around riders in those conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
Before opening a door when parked on the street, check sides and rear for bicyclists and open it with the hand nearer the center of the vehicle, a habit called the Dutch Reach. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
Check your path and blind spots for bicyclists before backing, changing lanes or turning, and before a left turn look for riders on the right side or shoulder and judge their speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A01
When a bicyclist is beside you as you prepare to turn right, slow down, yield and let the rider clear the intersection first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A01
Before a legal right turn on red, stop completely and look for bicyclists behind or beside you, turning left from across the street, or riding in the lane you will join. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A01
Do not honk near bicyclists unless a crash is about to happen, because the noise can startle them into crashing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists must hand-signal turns and stops but may be unable to when their skill or road conditions require both hands on the handlebars, so watch for head turns or shoulder checks as clues. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A01
A bicyclist signals a right turn with the right arm straight out or the left arm bent upward at a right angle, a left turn with the left arm straight out, and slowing or stopping with the left arm bent downward. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A01
Motorcyclists have the same rights and duties as other drivers but little crash protection, so a hit from a larger vehicle can injure or kill them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A01
Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width and often shift within it to see, be seen and avoid hazards, and strong wind can push one out of its lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A01
A two-wheeled motorcycle may lane filter past a stopped vehicle in its lane only when neighboring lanes are also stopped, there is room, and it moves no faster than 15 miles per hour. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A01
Motorcycles are small and hard to see, can speed up and stop faster than expected, and are endangered by road defects and debris, so use extra caution and a longer following distance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A02
Common bicycle collisions include a driver turning left in front of an oncoming rider, so look for riders on the shoulder or lane edge before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A02
Other common bicycle collisions come from running stop signs or signals, opening a door without looking back, riders going the wrong way against traffic, and drivers pulling out of driveways without looking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians, meaning people standing, walking, running or using mobility aids on public roads or private property, are the most vulnerable road users, and watching out for them is the driver's duty. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A02
Obey the speed limit or go slower when needed to spot and react to pedestrians, and remember that children and wheelchair users sit lower and are harder to see. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk, painted or not, and drivers must yield or stop completely to let them cross safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A02
When turning on red, be in the correct lane, stop completely and check for pedestrians in all directions before creeping forward to look for traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A02
Never stop with any part of your vehicle over the crosswalk, and never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, since its driver may be waiting for a pedestrian you cannot see. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A02
Watch for people getting in or out of parked cars, drive very carefully near schools, parks, parking lots, bus stops and events, and check mirrors and blind spots when backing out. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A02
Sharing the road is required by law, not just a safety habit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A02
A distraction is anything that takes your eyes, hands or mind off driving, and mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical ones; even tuning the radio is risky in bad weather or heavy traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A02
Do not eat, drink, read, smoke, vape, apply makeup or adjust music while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A02
Alcohol, marijuana and many other drugs reduce the ability to handle several tasks, so a distraction that is merely hazardous for a sober driver can be deadly for an impaired one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A02
Drivers may not use a mobile electronic device unless hands-free or in an emergency; careless driving caused by texting or other manual device use can bring a fine or a misdemeanor charge, so pull off the road to use a phone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F36 | anchor: A02
To prevent distraction, skip phone use and emotional conversations, restrain children properly, put pets in a carrier or kennel, learn your controls, preset radio stations and playlists, and plan your route before driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-F37 | anchor: A02
Aggressive driving is any willful behavior behind the wheel that endangers people or property without regard for safety. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]
